A robot just raised its fist at a Qualcomm keynote, collapsed face-first, and got covered with a tarp — while the presentation kept going.

Days after that collapse, investors handed NEURA Robotics one point four billion dollars anyway. The sim-to-real gap is real, it's on camera, and it's the same gap hiding inside every AI product being sold to you right now.

What you'll learn:
✅ Why "production ready" and "safe-collapse sequence" can't both be true
✅ The two NEURA stage failures — Munich 2025 and Taipei 2026 — and what they share
✅ How to build for AI failure before it costs you

The businesses winning with AI aren't the ones with the flashiest demo.
